proof_analysis: The supplier proof uses only its F2 stopping-time/stopped-sigma-algebra tests, F3 increasing filtration and deterministic-time adaptation, and F1 ambient-null inclusion. Brownian Gaussian laws, independent increments, Brownian natural-filtration minimality and right continuity never enter the three numbered proof steps.

For fixed t>0, upper rounding tau wedge t on its deterministic dyadic grid gives finite-valued stopping times rho_n<=t decreasing to tau wedge t. The coefficients X_q and event {rho_n=q} are F_q measurable, so X_(rho_n) is F_t measurable. A total measurable limit Z_t exists by assigning0 where the finite-vector limit fails.

On the one measurable full-probability continuity event and {tau<=t}, Z_t=X_tau. For each Borel C, the test {X_tau in C} intersect {tau<=t} differs from an F_t event by a subset of the ambient measurable continuity-null event. Requiring every such subset in F0 makes that difference measurable even before ambient measurability of X_tau has been established. This avoids a circular measurability assertion.

At t=T the argument makes X_tau ambient measurable, at t>T use F_T subset F_t, and at t=0 the relevant value is X0. These are exactly all stopped-sigma-algebra tests. The T=0, deterministic tau, zero-dimensional vector and empty continuity-exception cases are immediate instances. No selection beyond the retained inherited AC convention is used.

The phrase complete filtration can mean merely each F_t is complete under its restricted measure, which need not include every ambient null event at F0. Therefore the proposed hypothesis spells out ambient-null completeness instead of silently claiming the result for that weaker interpretation. Every usual filtered space in the actual SDE supplier meets the explicit stronger convention.
